analyzed_vuln.description: ProcessPosText dispatches into GlyphIdGlyphFinder for kGlyphID text without enforcing that the provided byteLength is a multiple of sizeof(SkGlyphID). GlyphIdGlyphFinder::nextGlyphId then reads a 16-bit glyph ID from *text unconditionally, so an odd/truncated glyph buffer causes a 2-byte read past the end (heap-buffer-overflow). The crash appears in nextGlyphId, but the root cause is missing length/alignment validation before selecting/using the GlyphID path.
analyzed_vuln.conditions: From the api_mock_gpu_canvas fuzz path, attacker-controlled picture/text commands reach drawPosText/drawPosTextH and then SkFindAndPlaceGlyph::ProcessPosText with TextEncoding::kGlyphID and a text pointer/byteLength pair. If byteLength is not an exact multiple of 2 (or otherwise allows a final partial glyph), the glyph iteration advances by glyph IDs and performs one extra 2-byte read at the tail, triggering OOB read in nextGlyphId.
